origin: A form Edward Tufte introduced in his 1983 book The Visual Display of Quantitative Information.
whenToUse: You compare only two points in time, such as last year and this year.
You highlight items whose rank changed.
whenNotToUse: There are three or more points in time (use a line chart).
There are so many items that the lines tangle.
Only sizes at one point are compared (use a bar chart).
accessibility: Values are written at both ends, so the slope doesn't have to be read.
Rises and falls show by line direction along with color.
Both values of every item are kept as a list for screen readers.
